titulo: AI Rout and Midterm Shocks Shake Global Markets
resumo: November brought intense volatility as markets digested a dramatic political shift and severe tech-sector shocks. **US midterms delivered a Democratic sweep**, upending policy expectations and triggering a massive tech sell-off. Compounding the turmoil, **Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang resigned amid scandals**, knocking confidence in the artificial intelligence boom. Meanwhile, **hot inflation data revived rate-hike fears**, pushing bond yields higher across the Atlantic. Equities managed some resilience, though defensive rotations and currency adjustments highlighted growing investor anxiety.

sumup.frase: Markets navigate political upheaval, **AI sector stress**, and renewed inflation fears.
sumup.porque: Investors balanced strong economic growth and mega-IPOs against regulatory threats and surging bond yields.

drivers.texto: The Democratic Party's capture of Congress triggered a historic one-day relief rally led by the Dow, but also sparked fears of heavy regulation and data center freezes. Renewable stocks surged on the news, while tech and traditional energy shares faced immediate headwinds.

Jensen Huang stepped down following an internal investigation into an affair with a suspected Chinese executive, erasing billions in market value. The sudden departure of the AI sector's standard-bearer rattled investor confidence and heightened scrutiny over chip export controls.

drivers.factor: Hot US Inflation and Rate Fears
drivers.texto: October consumer price data came in hotter than expected, igniting a new chorus of Federal Reserve rate-hike predictions. US Treasury 2-year yields rose 17bp on the month to 4.73, while 10-year yields added 4bp to 4.98.

drivers.factor: Brent Crude Tumbles on Middle East Hopes
drivers.texto: Crude oil plummeted 23.3% this month to 92.14 dollars a barrel as diplomatic progress and peace talks regarding Iran eased supply concerns. The slide in energy costs provided some relief to broader inflation pressures.

themes.texto: The artificial intelligence sector faced a historic reality check as political headwinds and regulatory scrutiny converged. Anthropic pressed ahead with a massive IPO target near 1.3 trillion to 1.4 trillion dollars, even as neocloud credit risks and soaring infrastructure costs spooked lenders. Bond yields for high-exposure firms surged, forcing a systemic re-evaluation of valuations across the technology landscape.

themes.titulo: Central Banks and Resurgent Inflation Pressures
themes.texto: Persistent inflation readings kept global monetary authorities on high alert, with US and UK policymakers signaling a potential return to tightening. Euro area inflation held at 4% in October, while Portugal's rate reached 3.9% with a 12-month average of 2.9%. Consequently, mortgage and term deposit rates remained elevated, impacting consumer borrowing and real estate markets.

themes.titulo: Global Currency and Bond Market Adjustments
themes.texto: Fixed income markets experienced sharp volatility as bond yields reacted to shifting fiscal outlooks and monetary policy chatter. The EUR/USD exchange rate fell 1.1% this month to 1.1052, reflecting relative economic pressures. Meanwhile, credit spreads tightened slightly, with the US high-yield spread dropping 14bp to 3.3, demonstrating lingering investor appetite for yield despite macroeconomic jitters.

questoes.q: Will the departure of Jensen Huang permanently derail the artificial intelligence infrastructure boom?
questoes.porque: Nvidia has been the undisputed linchpin of the global AI hardware supply chain and market sentiment.
questoes.sinais: Upcoming earnings and capital expenditure updates from major hyperscalers will reveal whether demand holds steady.

questoes.q: How will a newly Democratic Congress constrain big tech and data center expansion?
questoes.porque: Lawmakers have signaled aggressive oversight, potential export restrictions, and possible moratoriums on new data centers.
questoes.sinais: Legislative text and committee announcements regarding tech regulations in Washington.

questoes.q: Are central banks finished raising interest rates, or will hot inflation force another tightening cycle?
questoes.porque: Sticky inflation prints and strong job additions have revived fears of higher-for-longer monetary policy.
questoes.sinais: Incoming employment and consumer price index data releases over the coming months.

momentos.facto: Marvell agreed to acquire Lumentum in a multi-billion dollar AI connectivity deal.
Democrats swept Congress in the midterm elections, sparking a massive relief rally for the Dow Jones.
The Nasdaq suffered its worst daily drop since 2025 as a Democratic victory stoked AI regulation fears.
The Bank of England raised interest rates to 4%, marking its first increase in over three years.
US inflation printed hotter than expected, sending Treasury yields surging and reviving rate-hike bets.
Jensen Huang resigned as CEO of Nvidia, plunging tech stocks into further turmoil.
